concepts.title: South Asia: Geography and States
concepts.section: The Military and Administration in Pakistan
concepts.definition: South Asia comprises eight states - India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Afghanistan - with enormous demographic weight in India and varied political systems from stable democracies to military rules and monarchies.
concepts.key_idea: One region, many regimes: the subcontinent's states differ in size, systems and stability, which shapes every bilateral tie.

concepts.title: Pakistan, Bangladesh and Nepal's Politics
concepts.definition: Pakistan alternated civilian and military rule with the army dominating security policy; Bangladesh born in 1971 through liberation war oscillated between civilian rule and military interventions; Nepal moved from monarchy to constitutional democracy through popular movements and a republican constitution.
concepts.key_idea: Each state's civil-military balance decides its democracy's depth, and 1971 redrew the region's map and politics.

solution_steps.explain: military interventions repeatedly displaced civilian governments

concepts.title: India-Pakistan and Sri Lankan Conflicts
concepts.definition: India-Pakistan conflict centres on Kashmir, wars of 1947-48, 1965 and 1971 and nuclearisation after the 1998 tests; India-Sri Lanka relations involve the Tamil question and Indian intervention, while China's rise shapes strategic calculations across the region.
concepts.key_idea: Nuclear tests of 1998 made the subcontinent's central conflict more dangerous and more stable at once - deterrence with brinkmanship.

concepts.title: Cooperation: SAARC and Regional Peace
concepts.definition: South Asian cooperation runs through SAARC, founded in 1985 for collective self-reliance, and through trade and cultural exchanges; bilateral disputes, especially India-Pakistan, limit integration despite shared histories and democratisation trends across the region.
concepts.key_idea: SAARC shows both promise and paralysis: agreements exist, but the India-Pakistan freeze caps regional integration.
